subject: BrightLeaf: inference deployment qualification & cost brief
messages:

Subject: Post-call — BrightLeaf deployment needs and cost ask

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the call earlier — that was helpful. Quick recap of our environment and an ask for rough economics so we can compare deployment modes before we bring in procurement/security:

Environment highlights:
- Production target: 15 sustained requests/sec (QPS) with short daily peaks to ~45–55 QPS for bursts (30–90s).
- Average token budget per request: ~350 tokens (rough split: 100 input / 250 output).
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms ideally, 500ms max.
- Data sensitivity: user PII and health-related content; we need to evaluate VPC or on-prem.
- Retention: logs/metrics retained 90 days; no long-term user content storage acceptable without DPA.

Asks: could you send a short, comparative cost model for: Hosted API (pay-as-you-go), Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit), and Private (VPC-managed or on-prem) including one-time/onboarding costs? Please include assumptions about token counts, useful efficiency levers (caching, prefix reuse, quantization), and which model variants you’d recommend for our latency/throughput profile.

We’d like a short one-page TCO we can share internally (product + infra + procurement). Also can you flag the items security will want to review for a VPC/on-prem path?

Thanks — Samira

--
Samira Khan
VP of Product
BrightLeaf AI

Samira — great to connect. Drafted a short comparative brief and attached a simple TCO workbook (BrightLeaf_TCO_v1.xlsx) plus a one-pager (Redwood_Pricing_Summary.pdf). Below are the high-level ballparks and assumptions so you have something to take to your procurement team.

Assumptions used (please flag if any are off):
- Sustained: 15 req/sec, average 350 tokens/req => ~13.6B tokens/month (see workbook for step-by-step).
- Peak headroom: dedicated sizing recommended to support steady-state + autoscale for 45–55 QPS short bursts.
- Efficiency: we assume 0% caching baseline; enabling prefix/KV caching and light quantization can reduce billed tokens by ~20–30% for many chat-like workloads (we show a scenario at -25%).

1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) — fastest path to production
- Pricing assumption: $3.00 per million tokens (combined input+output).
- Baseline monthly cost (no caching): 13,608M tokens * $3.00 = $40,824/month.
- With 25% effective token reduction: ~ $30,618/month.
- Pros: no infra commit, fastest onboarding, Redwood handles infra, built-in fallbacks and model variants.
- Cons: less network isolation; may be unacceptable for regulated PII without add-on controls (we can discuss Private options).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — committed pool for predictable throughput
- Typical reserved pool that matches your sustained plus burst headroom: 6–8 vGPUs (model-dependent).
- Reservation pricing example: $35k/month for baseline reserved pool (covers sustained + modest burst via burst buffer).
- Effective unit cost: for heavy workloads the per-token effective cost can drop ~25–40% vs hosted because GPU utilization is higher and we avoid per-request platform overhead.
- Add-on for guaranteed p95 SLA and priority routing: +$3–5k/month.
- Pros: predictable monthly spend, capacity isolation, easier to satisfy compliance with dedicated tenancy.
- Cons: annual or quarterly commit often required for best rates; resizing takes time unless you add burst options.

3) Private (VPC-managed or on-prem) — maximum data control
- VPC-managed (Redwood control plane, customer VPC): one-time onboarding & network setup ~$25k, plus managed infra fee ~$10k/month + baseline GPU infra similar to Dedicated (or customer-provided).
- On-prem (air-gapped): professional services + packaging ~$250k one-time, then support/license ~$20k+/month depending on size.
- Pros: strongest data locality/isolation and control; necessary for regulated data or strict contractual requirements.
- Cons: higher up-front investment and longer lead times.

Quick sensitivity examples are in the workbook (attached).

Next steps I recommend:
- 1) Quick sync (30–45m) with your infra & security (we’ll bring our VPC checklist) — to confirm VPC vs on-prem trade-offs and network constraints.
- 2) If procurement wants numbers for a multi-quarter commit, we can model 6/12/24 month commits and show break-even vs hosted.
- 3) Run a 2-week pilot on our hosted environment using a small commit to validate latency and effective token counts (we’ll whitelist sample traffic and apply caching rules).

Would you be available Wed Jul 9 between 9–11am PT or Thu Jul 10 8–11am PT for a working session? Monica and Rishi are copied to help with sizing and pricing details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

- Our peaks are likely to be spikier than we said on the call; engineering expects occasional 60–70 QPS bursts (10–20s) during promotional traffic. Can Dedicated with burst buffers cover that or do we need to combine Dedicated + hosted fallback?
- We need p95 <= 200ms on the shortest path for a core flow — what model variants do you recommend and can you share examples of p95 you’ve measured on Dedicated vs Hosted for similar token lengths?
- Security: please include a short checklist for our security lead (network ports, KMS integration, audit logs retention, SCIM/SAML, data residency).

Availability: I can do Thu Jul 10 at 9:30am PT or Fri Jul 11 after 11am PT. Also please share the TCO workbook in XLSX (we got the PDF already).

—Samira

Short answers:
- Burst handling: Dedicated + short-hosted fallback is a common pattern. Dedicated pool sized for sustained traffic + buffer for modest bursts; configure automatic fallback to hosted model variants during long spikes. We’ll show a sample policy in the working session.
- Latency: for ~350 token workloads we typically see p95 in the 120–350ms range on Dedicated for optimized kernels (model dependent). Hosted p95 is similar for the same models but can vary more across multi-tenant hotspots. We’ll include observed p95 examples for two model variants in the deck.
- Security checklist (high level) included in workbook: VPC peering & endpoints, private subnets for inference, KMS/HSM integration for keys, audit logging (90d default), SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, SOC2 evidence pointers. For on-prem we list extra items (airgap install plan, physical security).

Meeting invite: I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu 7/10 9:30am PT and include Monica and Rishi. For the working session please include your security/infrastructure lead and procurement.

Action items (we will):
- Share XLSX TCO workbook (done) and one-pager (done).
- Prepare a dedicated vs hosted latency/p95 slide with measured samples.
- Draft a 2-week pilot plan and a sample short SOW (DocuSign link attached).

If you want us to pre-run a small synthetic load to show p95 on a matched model, let us know the exact prompt size and concurrency pattern and we’ll schedule it before the call.

See you Thu — Neha
